title: Shape Compare
description: Turn a square and compare its corners with a circle. A 3D setting adds a side view of the same two shapes.
learningObjectives: Identify a square by its four sides and four corners
Compare a front view with a side view of the same shapes

params.description: 2d shows one view. 3d adds a side view of the same shapes.

events.name: shapes_compared
events.description: The child compared the shapes on the page.

tutorGuide.intro: Turn the square. Then see how it compares with the circle.
steps: Count the corners on the square and on the circle.
If a side view appears, look at the same shapes from the side.
observationPrompts: How many corners does the square have after the turn?
What does the side view look like?

misconceptions.belief: Turning a shape gives it new sides.
misconceptions.response: A turn moves the shape. The square still has four sides and four corners.

hints: The labeled square is shape A.
A square has four corners. A circle has none.

accessibility.screenReaderSummary: A square and a circle. Turn the square, then compare their corners. A 3D setting adds a side view of the same shapes.
